sections.title: First: Executive Summary — Key Analyses
sections.content: This report analyzes 241 complaints recorded in the Customer Relationship Management system of the Fujairah General Police Command throughout the year 2025. These complaints represent genuine communications from customers regarding their experience with police, security, traffic, and correctional facility services. They form an organizational memory that has not yet been utilized to develop services and improve the customer journey.

subsections.title: Key Findings
subsections.content: Core Message: The complaints data reveals that the challenge is not the absence of digital channels — both the Ministry of Interior app and the Fujairah Police app are available for most services — but rather three obstacles: lack of proactive confirmation and updates on complaint status, weak digital guidance that causes customers to use the wrong channel, and a genuine service gap in objecting to traffic violations which requires physical presence. Addressing these three areas alone is capable of reducing complaint volume by more than 35%.

rows.Finding: 43% of complaints have no specific service classification
rows.Description: The system recorded 103 complaints under "Other", which hinders root-cause analysis and indicates a gap in the classification structure

rows.Finding: 39% of rejected cases are duplicate complaints
rows.Description: Customers resubmit the same complaint multiple times due to the absence of confirmation and updates

rows.Finding: 18% of rejections are reports submitted through the wrong channel
rows.Description: 16 cases were rejected because the customer used the complaints system to file a criminal report instead of the smart app — an awareness gap

rows.Finding: Traffic violation objections have no digital channel
rows.Description: The service is only available at the service center between 7:30–15:30, forcing customers to travel physically with no digital alternative
234 out of 241 complaints are closed within the specified timeframe according to the complaints management methodology, confirming processing efficiency after correct registration

subsections.title: 2.2  Classification Methodology
subsections.content:
The analysis relies on two primary references: the official complaints management methodology issued by the Fujairah General Police Command and the official service directory documenting the channels and requirements of each service. The official methodology classified complaints into three types based on complexity:
← Urgent/Critical Complaint: With clear procedures — closed within 24 hours
← Regular/Routine Complaint: Involving more than one department — closed within 5 working days
← Complex Complaint: Lengthy procedures or multiple entities — closed within 15 working days

subsections.title: 2.3  Analyzed Fields
subsections.content: The analysis included structured fields: service, main service, request severity, submission channel, status, department, nationality, and creation and closure dates. In-depth analysis required reading unstructured text fields: request details and resolution text — as these fields reveal root causes that do not appear in the structural classification, such as actual reasons for rejection and repetition patterns.

subsections.title: 3.2  Submission Channel Analysis — 91% of Requests Arrive via Digital Channels
subsections.content: Notably, 91% of complaints arrived via digital channels (64% mobile app, 27% website), proving that customers are digitally engaged and ready to interact through smart channels. However, digital arrival does not mean digital resolution — as most friction points center on the post-submission stage.

subsections.title: 3.3  Processing Response Analysis — Rejection, Acceptance, and Duplication
subsections.content: The overall rejection rate reached 37% (90 complaints), a number that appears high at first glance, but an in-depth reading of decision texts reveals that 61% of this rejection is systemic in nature and does not reflect a service failure:

sections.title: Fourth: Second Analysis — Challenges in the Customer Journey
sections.content:
In-depth analysis of unstructured texts — request details and decision texts — reveals 7 critical friction points driving the majority of complaint volume. Most center around a single stage: post-submission. The customer arrives digitally with ease, but loses follow-up thereafter.
Critical Discovery: 39 duplicate complaints — representing 16% of total complaints — could have been entirely prevented with a single action: sending an automatic text message with a reference number upon receiving the complaint and when updating the request status with clear resolution reasons for the customer. The customer does not repeat because they are unhappy, but because they do not know whether their complaint was received. This single action alone would immediately reduce the apparent volume of complaints by more than 16%.

rows.Friction Point: Absence of immediate confirmation after complaint submission in some cases
rows.Root Cause: Customer is unsure whether their complaint was received in some cases — resubmits multiple times
rows.Improvement Action: Review automated notification system and ensure that a notification with a reference number is sent upon receipt (within 60 seconds)

rows.Friction Point: Submitting a criminal report via the complaints system
rows.Root Cause: Customer does not distinguish between a report and a complaint — uses whichever is nearest
rows.Improvement Action: Smart guidance window: "Do you want to file a report? Click here"

rows.Root Cause: Customer is surprised by their report being closed without prior notification
rows.Improvement Action: Mandatory notification upon report archiving with a brief explanation of the reason

rows.Friction Point: Non-enforcement of arrest warrants and court rulings
rows.Root Cause: Customer files a complaint to pressure enforcement instead of using an official channel, due to not being informed of the reason for case closure
rows.Improvement Action: Create a portal or system to track request status with clear explanation of the status and reason for request closure

rows.Friction Point: Issues with organizing visits to correctional facilities
rows.Root Cause: Lack of clarity regarding the steps for submitting a request via the app and scheduling appointments
rows.Improvement Action: Improve UX for the visit service in the Fujairah Police app + FAQ

rows.Friction Point: Traffic violation objections with no digital channel
rows.Root Cause: The service requires physical presence during working hours only
rows.Improvement Action: Develop a digital service in accordance with terms and regulations (roadmap priority)

rows.Friction Point: Using complaints to inquire about the status of a previous request
rows.Root Cause: No easy complaint tracking portal — customer files a complaint instead of making an inquiry
rows.Improvement Action: Unified tracking portal: "Where is my complaint?" by simply entering the reference number

sections.title: Fifth: Third Analysis — Digital Gap Analysis
sections.content:
Why do complaints persist despite the availability of the Ministry of Interior smart app and the Fujairah Police app? This section answers with a scientific approach built on the official service directory: for each service that is the subject of a complaint, its profile in the directory is examined to determine whether the gap is a genuine digital gap or an awareness gap.
Core Discovery: Most services leading in complaint volume — such as filing criminal reports, good conduct certificates, and organizing visits — have actual digital channels documented in the service directory. The gap therefore is not in building new channels, but in raising customer awareness about using what already exists — with the exception of one service that has no digital alternative yet: objection to traffic violations.

sections.title: Sixth: Fourth Analysis — Digital Transformation Plan

subsections.title: 6.1  Priority FAQs (Extracted from Actual Complaints Data)
subsections.title_en: 6.1  Priority FAQs (Extracted from Actual Complaints Data)
subsections.content: These questions are extracted from the most frequently contacted services in the complaints data. The answers are based on service cards in the official service directory of the Fujairah General Police Command — not on staff procedural practice. The objective is to provide the customer with the correct path before submitting a complaint.

rows.Question: How do I file a criminal report?
rows.Official Channel: MOI App or Ministry of Interior website (24/7) or Service Center
rows.Correct Answer: Via the Ministry of Interior app (MOI): select "Criminal Reports", enter your ID and UAE PASS, and fill in the incident details. The service is free and available 24 hours, 7 days a week.

rows.Question: How do I object to a traffic violation?
rows.Official Channel: Service Center only (7:30–15:30) — no digital option currently available
rows.Correct Answer: Visit the Traffic Services Center in person between 7:30–15:30 with your ID, driving license, vehicle ownership card, and violations statement. The service is free and takes 5 minutes.

rows.Question: How do I request a visit for an inmate at a correctional facility?
rows.Correct Answer: Via the Fujairah Police app: select "Organize Visits", enter the ID number, specify the visit type (family / lawyer / embassy). The service is free.

rows.Question: How do I obtain a good conduct certificate?
rows.Official Channel: MOI App + Ministry website (24/7) — 5 minutes only
rows.Correct Answer: Via the Ministry of Interior app (MOI): select "Good Conduct Certificate", enter your ID. The service is fully electronic and takes 5 minutes. Check fees upon submission.

rows.Question: How do I file a complaint about an employee or procedure at a police station?
rows.Correct Answer: Submit your complaint via the Ministry of Interior and Fujairah Police app or website under the "Contact Us" tab. You will receive a reference number immediately upon submission, and the standard response period is 5 working days.

rows.Question: What should I do if I have not received a response to an old complaint?
rows.Official Channel: Do not resubmit — contact using the reference number
rows.Correct Answer: Do not resubmit the complaint — use the reference number to inquire via the Ministry app or call the unified call center. Resubmission is classified as a "duplicate complaint" and is closed automatically.

subsections.title: 6.2  Path to Eliminating 55+ Complaint Cases via Proactive Notifications
subsections.title_en: 6.2  Path to Eliminating 55+ Complaint Cases via Proactive Notifications
subsections.content: The analysis estimates that at least 55 complaints — representing 23% of the total — could have been entirely avoided with a simple proactive notification system. This is not complex technology: a single SMS upon receipt, a brief update upon transfer, and a notification upon closure with the reason — and that is sufficient to remove the motivation for repetition.

rows.Expected Impact: Substantial reduction in duplicate complaints — eliminates the main motivation for repetition

sections.title: Seventh: AI-Powered Use Cases
sections.content:
The Fujairah General Police Command has more than 241 documented complaint records with detailed texts and processing decisions — a training dataset ready for building customized AI models. The analysis estimates that 40%+ of complaint volume is eligible for partial or full automated processing.
Key Note: The AI training data already exists in the CRM system — 241 documented complaints with their texts and decisions form a genuine starting point, expanding daily as work continues. Automated classification alone solves the most pressing problems.

rows.Function: Classifies the complaint at the moment of submission: service complaint / criminal report / employment grievance / out-of-jurisdiction
rows.Expected Impact: Elimination of 90% of rejection cases due to misclassification

rows.Expected Impact: 30% reduction in complaints resulting from confusion

sections.title: Eighth: Proposed Improvement Roadmap
sections.content: This roadmap consolidates the recommendations from all four analyses into a prioritized system according to impact and ease of implementation. Immediate items do not require new technologies — they are procedural improvements and configuration of existing systems. Medium and long-term items represent the real investment in digital transformation.

rows.Recommendation: Improve SMS notifications upon complaint receipt, status update, and closure with a reference number
Activate a smart guidance window upon complaint submission: "Do you want to file a report?"
Develop a service chatbot linked to the official service directory
rows.Expected Impact: Automatic redirection of 25% of guidance complaints

rows.Recommendation: Improve user experience of the visits service in the Fujairah Police app + visual FAQ
Develop a digital traffic violation objection form (genuine gap)
Develop an AI-powered automated complaint classification module
Unified tracking portal: "Where is my complaint? / Where is my report?" on a single page

tables.caption: This roadmap consolidates the recommendations from all four analyses into a prioritized system according to impact and ease of implementation. rows.Expected Complaint: I have not received any confirmation that my complaint was received
rows.Impact: If the absence of confirmation continues, the number of duplicate complaints will increase cumulatively, burdening the system with redundant requests of no operational value, and causing the customer to lose confidence that their communications are even being received.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Send an automatic SMS immediately upon complaint registration, including the request number and receipt date
• Add a confirmation email within 5 minutes of creation

rows.Expected Complaint: Weeks have passed since my report and I do not know its progress
rows.Impact: If updates on security complaints continue to be absent, procedural ambiguity will turn into escalating tension that may push customers toward media escalation or legal channels, bypassing the official process.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Create a tracking portal allowing customers to view the complaint stage without revealing investigation details
• Send an automatic notification every 7 days with a status update, even if it only says "under processing"
• Define the average processing duration and publish it to manage customer expectations

rows.Expected Complaint: My complaint was rejected because it is not within Fujairah's jurisdiction
rows.Impact: If customers remain without clear guidance, police resources will continue to absorb complaints outside their authority, and customers' sense of being referred from one entity to another without resolution will deepen.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Publish a digital guide specifying the jurisdiction of each government entity in Fujairah — an awareness initiative
• Send a referral message including contact information for the competent authority

rows.Expected Complaint: My traffic violation objection was rejected without a clear path forward
rows.Impact: If the objection path remains ambiguous, repeated traffic complaints will accumulate and the sense of procedural injustice will become a negative influence on the entity's image in the licensing sector.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Document objection procedures on a dedicated page with numbered steps
• Notify the customer of the decision within a specified period with the legal justification stated

rows.Expected Complaint: I submitted a request and was not responded to within the specified timeframe
rows.Impact: If SLA violations continue without systemic handling, the compliance rate will gradually decline until the exception becomes the norm, which will negatively impact indicators in supervisory reports.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Prepare an internal Dashboard alerting officials to any request approaching its deadline
• Ensure that SLA violations trigger automatic escalation to the direct supervisor
• Determine whether cases are concentrated in a specific department

rows.Expected Complaint: I do not know whether my good conduct certificate is ready or not
rows.Impact: If certificate complaints remain without a clear tracking path, unnecessary personal visits and phone inquiries will increase, forming an operational burden that can be entirely avoided.
rows.Proposed Proactive Solution:
• Send an SMS immediately upon completion of certificate or permit preparation
• Add request status tracking via national ID number on the official app
• Publish the standard processing duration for each certificate type at communication points

sections.title: Ninth: Conclusion — From Data to Decision
sections.content: Final Message: The 2025 complaints embody a dual picture: a General Command that closes 97% of its complaints within specified deadlines, while at the same time customers repeat their complaints four times because they have not received a response. The contradiction is not in service quality, but in the gap between what happens internally and what the customer perceives. Closing this gap — through proactive notification, smart guidance, and automated classification — is the investment with the fastest return and deepest impact on the customer journey with the Fujairah Police.

rows.Pillar One: Precision: Activate smart classification at submission to distinguish between complaints, reports, and grievances
rows.Pillar Two: Accessibility: Deploy a proactive notification system at every stage: receipt ← transfer ← closure
rows.Pillar Three: Intelligence: Build an automated classifier trained on actual CRM data to classify complaints in real time

rows.Pillar One: Precision: Close the genuine digital gap by developing a digital traffic violation objection form
rows.Pillar Two: Accessibility: A unified tracking portal combining complaints and reports in a single interface for the customer
rows.Pillar Three: Intelligence: A chatbot linked to the service directory to automatically redirect guidance complaints (30%+ of volume)

rows.Pillar One: Precision: Review the service classification structure to reduce the "Other" percentage from 43% to less than 10%
rows.Pillar Two: Accessibility: Extend visit service hours in the Fujairah Police app and improve user experience
rows.Pillar Three: Intelligence: A pattern detection system to proactively monitor repetition of complaints for a specific department or service
